```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os, sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Make the helpers beside this file importable, plus python_style_util one level up.
HERE = os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(HERE))   # ..parent (python_style_util.py in this repo)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)                     # this folder (deck_utils.py, brand_palettes.py)

from python_style_util import p, f, s, C, chart_title   # chart_title = styled left title
from deck_utils import deck_style, add_baseline, strip_bar_labels, small_labels, reset_labels
from brand_palettes import HOMESTART, JACARANDA   # named colours to hand-pick from

PAL = deck_style()                 # ← swap to deck_style(theme="homestart")
# Colour a chart either way:
#   • Automatic : PAL.primary / PAL.secondary / PAL.tertiary / PAL.ramp  (follow the theme)
#   • Hand-pick : a specific brand colour, e.g. HOMESTART.salmon, JACARANDA.gold

# ── DEMO DATA — delete this block and load your own (df = pd.read_csv(...)) ──
seg  = ["Segment A", "Segment B", "Segment C", "Segment D", "Segment E"]
val  = [12.4, 9.1, 7.8, 6.2, 4.5]
val2 = [3.0, 4.2, 6.1, 5.0, 7.3]
BASE = 0.081                        # a reference rate, if you use add_baseline()
```

## Single chart {data-kick="Example · one chart"}

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.6))
colors = [PAL.ramp(v / max(val)) for v in val]              # graded light→dark by height
bars = ax.bar(seg, val, color=colors, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", padding=4, fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=11, color=C.text)
chart_title(ax, "One chart, centred on a card")
ax.set_ylabel("Demo metric"); ax.margins(y=0.16)
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — graded colour (`PAL.ramp`), value labels (`ax.bar_label`) and a styled
title (`chart_title`) are what make it read as finished. A flat `ax.bar(…, color=PAL.primary)`
also works when you want it plain.
:::

## Three panels, one figure {data-kick="Example · multi-panel"}

```{python}
# Best when the panels are the same chart repeated. One image, fills the card.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.7))
colors = [PAL.ramp(v / max(val)) for v in val]
for ax, t in zip(axes, ["Panel one", "Panel two", "Panel three"]):
    bars = ax.bar(seg, val, color=colors, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
    ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", padding=3, fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=9, color=C.text)
    chart_title(ax, t)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.margins(y=0.18)
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — `plt.subplots(1, 3, …)`; keep the total figsize wide-and-short (~3:1).
:::

## Two figures side by side {data-kick="Example · two-up"}

```{python}
#| layout-ncol: 2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 4.4))
bars = ax.bar(seg, val, color=[PAL.ramp(v / max(val)) for v in val], edgecolor="white", linewidth=1)
ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", padding=3, fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=10, color=C.text)
chart_title(ax, "A bar chart")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); ax.margins(y=0.18); plt.show()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.2, 4.4))
ax.plot(seg, val2, marker="o", color=PAL.secondary, linewidth=2.5)
chart_title(ax, "A trend line")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45); plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — `#| layout-ncol: 2` puts two independent figures on their own cards.
:::

## A text slide {data-kick="Example · text"}

Text-only slides centre themselves — no layout work needed. Use these for
context, method, or a recommendation.

- **Retained** — the drivers you're keeping
- **Parked** — what you set aside, and why
- **Next** — the one action you're asking for

::: {.caveat}
EXAMPLE — `.caveat` (accent) for a watch-out; `.takeaway` (primary) for the key point.
:::

## Using the shared chart helpers {data-kick="Example · helpers"}

```{python}
# The default_rate_by_bin helper (from credit_utils) + add_baseline / strip_bar_labels:
# fig, axes = default_rate_by_bin(df, ["FEATURE"], "TARGET",
#     grade_scale=PAL.ramp, show_base_rate=False, panel_w=5.0, panel_h=4.7)
# add_baseline(axes, BASE)     # reference line, label parked in the margin
# strip_bar_labels(axes)       # drop per-bar labels on dense (12-bin) panels
# plt.show()
#
# Here's the same idea by hand — a graded bar using the theme ramp:
import matplotlib.cm as cm
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.6))
norm = plt.Normalize(min(val), max(val))
ax.bar(seg, val, color=[PAL.ramp(norm(v)) for v in val])
add_baseline([ax], BASE)
ax.set_title("Graded bars coloured by height (PAL.ramp)", loc="left")
plt.show()
```

::: {.takeaway}
EXAMPLE — `PAL.ramp` is a colormap; `PAL.ramp(0..1)` gives a colour along it.
:::
